artifact.title: One central partial involution generates a positive cone of viable A-B repairs

centralDatum.Q: Q=P_A-P_B on each left/right bimodule action
centralDatum.consequence: The support projector S is a polynomial in Q, not an independent structure.

basisOperators.deformation: Delta V=M0^2(kappa_U U+kappa_P P), with kappa_U,kappa_P nonnegative

interpretation: Every positive mixture interpolates between exact selectivity and algebraic simplicity without introducing a new projector.
Projected strength stabilizes G without distorting desired B-other condensates; unrestricted strength contributes slightly less efficiently but may be easier to generate.
A UV calculation need only land inside a broad convex region rather than reproduce one exact coefficient.
dynamicsOptions: Treat Q as fixed finite-geometric data satisfying Q^3=Q.
Promote Q to a constrained compensator whose norm condition Q^2=S is enforced kinematically.
Use a stiff potential for Q^2-S, accepting and then bounding radial backreaction.
Identify Q with a discrete remnant of a larger broken internal symmetry.
scope: The cone uses the preferred carrier's exact radial stability inequality and assumes no additional invariants.
Nonnegative coefficients guarantee bounded quadratic contributions; negative mixtures may enlarge the viable region but are not classified.
Radiative closure of the two-operator basis has not been established.
falsifiers: Renormalization necessarily generates a third independent commutator invariant that destabilizes the cone.
The exact algebra quotient forbids Q while separately admitting P_A and P_B.
A UV completion fixes coefficients outside both the lower stability half-plane and the upper weak-amplitude bound.
Dynamical Q backreaction invalidates the fixed-Q coefficient map.
next: Compute the one-loop mixing matrix between U and P.
Build a stiff-Q toy potential and quantify backreaction on kappa_U and the desired condensates.

artifact.conclusion: A single central partial involution Q organizes both successful repairs. Their positive mixtures occupy a simple convex viability cone, making coefficient generation substantially less restrictive than either endpoint suggests.

artifact.title: Product compensator toy unifies Spin(2,3) coframe breaking with the finite A-B repair

Its value is that it turns the required mass from an appended potential term into a direct test of the claimed Spin(2,3)-relational unification.

artifact.title: The unrestricted central commutator passes the full real Hessian at delta=2/5

comparison.unrestrictedRational: At delta=2/5, the natural leakage is compensated and every audited inactive real mode is strictly massive.
comparison.tradeoff: The unrestricted completion uses less algebraic projection but shifts desired condensate magnitudes and has a small 3/500 stability margin.

implications: The natural unprojected commutator is locally viable in the complete real inactive-field sector.
Its 2/5 coefficient is a simple rational target and eliminates the marginal X/G modes present at the minimal projected threshold.
The small lowest eigenvalue makes radiative and complex-direction corrections quantitatively decisive rather than merely formal.

The exact one-form quotient and canonical spacetime kinetic normalization are still provisional.

Loop running shifts the light fourfold mode negative before matching to the low-energy theory.

The normalized compensator construction fixes delta below 24/61 or a leakage ratio above the derived wedge.
